The best free image resizers

Resizing a folder of photos for a website, an email or an application form should be quick and free. These three tools all do batches; they differ in options, limits and whether your photos leave your computer.

We make Slop Resize, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • Free, without a cap on how many pictures
  • Photos stay on your device
  • Ways to set the size: pixels, percentage, long edge, file size, crop
  • Output formats and extras

1. Slop Resize (ours)

Best for: Batches that must fit a size or a file limit, such as under 100 KB, and videos too, without uploading.

Good

  • Finds the highest quality that fits a file size limit
  • Fit, cover, stretch and fit-inside, with an anchor; presets for social, email and 4K
  • Resizes videos to MP4 or WebM with the audio kept
  • Saved presets; results download in a ZIP
  • Works on your phone, tablet and computer in the browser, even offline

Not so good

  • Still in beta
  • No smart crop with focal point detection, batch renaming or watermark
  • A file size limit needs JPEG, WebP or AVIF; PNG only gets smaller with fewer pixels
  • Big batches take longer on older computers

Open Slop Resize

2. BIRME

Best for: Cropping a batch to one exact size with a smart focal point, plus renaming and watermarks.

Good

  • Processes images locally; nothing is uploaded, by its own description
  • Smart crop with automatic focal point, or a custom crop per image
  • Extras: text and image watermarks, borders, batch rename, ZIP or folder save
  • AI background removal and 2× to 4× super-resolution

Not so good

  • Its pages do not mention resizing by percentage or to a file size
  • Pictures only, no video
  • The page carries ads

BIRME website · Sources: BIRME home

3. iLoveIMG

Best for: A quick online resize of up to 30 files, with Google Drive and Dropbox import.

Good

  • Resize by pixels or percentage, keep the aspect ratio, never enlarge
  • Imports from Google Drive and Dropbox
  • Part of a set of image tools, with an API

Not so good

  • Free tasks are limited to 30 files and 200 MB, with ads
  • Files are uploaded and processed on its servers
  • Cropping is a separate tool

iLoveIMG website · Sources: iLoveIMG resize, iLoveIMG pricing, iLoveIMG security, iLoveIMG photo editor

Which one to choose

Slop Resize is our pick for this page's criteria: no cap, nothing uploaded, and the most ways to set the size, including a file size limit, plus video.

Choose BIRME if you need to crop a batch to one exact size with smart crop, renaming and watermarks; it is just as private. Choose iLoveIMG for a quick online job of up to 30 files from Google Drive or Dropbox.

Questions

How do I resize many images at once for free?

All three do batches. Slop Resize and BIRME have no stated limit and work in your browser; iLoveIMG takes up to 30 files per free task.

Can I resize a photo to under 100 KB?

Slop Resize has a Maximum file size setting that finds the best quality under your limit. BIRME and iLoveIMG do not mention a file size target on their pages.

Are my photos uploaded?

Slop Resize and BIRME resize in your browser. iLoveIMG processes files on its servers and deletes them within two hours.

Can I resize a video too?

Slop Resize resizes videos to MP4 or WebM and keeps the sound. BIRME is for pictures only.
